questions.q: What is the strongest single artifact for summarizing the Summit Ridge project?
options: A before-and-after table of baseline versus final measures, each verified by a query
A screenshot of the Data Loader window
A list of every SOQL keyword used
The raw export CSV
questions.explain: A short before-and-after table with verified numbers tells the whole story at a glance.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the five parts of the portfolio presentation?
options: A full record-by-record listing of all 41,860 Leads
The problem, with the counts
The approach
The result and the lesson
questions.explain: The five parts are problem, approach, key queries, safety design, and result. A record-level listing is not part of it.

questions.q: Why is the Summit Ridge project safe to show in a portfolio?
options: It uses a fictional company and dataset, unlike real customer data
Salesforce data can never be shown outside the org
Data Loader removes identifying values automatically
It has no real queries in it
questions.explain: Because the company and data are fictional, nothing identifying is exposed. With real employer work, remove customer names and emails first.

questions.q: Which recommendation directly prevents new spellings of 'Trade Show' from entering LeadSource?
options: Restrict the LeadSource picklist so values outside its list are rejected
Run the dedupe query every year
Delete the LeadSource field
Convert all Leads to Contacts
questions.explain: A restricted picklist rejects values not on its defined list, which stops imports adding stray spellings.

questions.q: Which course comes next in the Salesforce Data Analyst path after SOQL & Salesforce Data Management?
options: Salesforce Reports & Dashboards
Advanced Data Loader
Apex Triggers
Terraform & Bicep
questions.explain: The path continues with Salesforce Reports & Dashboards, which presents trustworthy data to the people who use it.
